queries.query: "Aad Meewisse Exclusive" Bergschenhoek AND (assimilatiebelichting OR groeilicht OR "belichte teelt")
queries.content:
Aad Meewisse Exclusive is a rose-growing operation located in Bergschenhoek, Netherlands, at Hoeksekade 157.[5][7] The company is part of the Meewisse Roses enterprise, which specializes in cultivating high-quality red roses, particularly the Red Naomi variety.

## Company Background and Innovation

Aad Meewisse founded his rose-growing business in 1981 and has been a pioneer in adopting advanced horticultural techniques.[1][3] One of his most significant innovations was being among the first horticulturists to implement **assimilation lighting (assimilatiebelichting)** in rose cultivation, beginning in 1988.[1] This technology allows for year-round production by supplementing natural daylight with artificial grow lights during periods of low natural light.

## Production and Operations

The Bergschenhoek facility operates as a state-of-the-art growing operation with 43,000 square meters of growing area.[1] The company produces approximately 13 million roses annually using 25 dedicated employees.[1] The operation exclusively focuses on cultivating the Red Naomi rose variety, which has proven to be highly successful in the market.[1][3]

## Sustainability and Quality

The company emphasizes sustainable practices through the use of **biological crop protection** methods rather than chemical pesticides.[1][3] The facility has been designed to minimize energy consumption and waste while improving working conditions. These innovations have enabled Meewisse Roses to maintain top-quality rose production that meets international standards.[1]

Tom Meewisse, Aad's son, joined the family business after graduating from the University of Applied Sciences and continues to uphold the company's commitment to quality and innovation.[1]
